Peterson, II, p. 79: according to a.Dig. Kathākośa, Akalaṅka an. Niṣkalaṅka were the two sons of King Śubhatuṅga of Mānyakheṭa, i. e. Kṛṣṇarāja, the Rāṣṭrakūṭa King, 753-755 A. D. Akalaṅka then became a monk. See also Yaśastilakacampūvyākhyā, p. 236. K.

The Kanarese work Rājāvalikathe, 8th section, gives the story of Akalaṅka an. Himaśītala. Here father given a. a. Arhaddvija an. brother Niṣkalaṅka; studied under a Bauddha named Bhagavaddāsa; fought the Śaivas a. Sudhāpura.
